# Nexis AI — 30-Day AI Governance & Pilot Diagnostic

> Plain-text summary for AI agents and search engines.

## Overview
Nexis AI is an executive healthcare technology advisory firm based in Ellicott City, Maryland, founded by Shafiq Rahman, MS, MBA, MCS, PMP® (Former Maryland State CIO). Nexis AI offers a single, fixed-price engagement: the "30-Day AI Governance & Pilot Diagnostic."

## Who Nexis AI Serves (Target Buyer)
Nexis AI serves exclusively:
- The CEO, COO, or Board Chair of a 100–400-bed community hospital or small health system.
- Geography: Maryland, District of Columbia, Pennsylvania, and Virginia.
- Operating environment: Hospitals that have NO full-time CIO (or operate with an interim CIO or IT director) and run Epic or MEDITECH as their electronic health record (EHR) platform.
- Situation: The hospital already has department-level AI tools or vendor pilots running without a single governed inventory of what is in use, who owns it, and what it costs.

## The Three Core Problems Solved
1. Departmental AI Sprawl: AI pilots are running in different departments with no single inventory.
2. Unclear Accountability & Risk: Nobody can say which pilots are safe to scale, which should be stopped, and who is accountable if one goes wrong.
3. Unanchored Board Spending: The board is being asked to approve AI spending without a risk-tiered, costed list.

## The Offer: 30-Day AI Governance & Pilot Diagnostic
- Engagement Name: 30-Day AI Governance & Pilot Diagnostic
- Fixed Price: $6,500 USD, one-time fee.
- Payment Terms: 50% due on booking, 50% due on delivery of the findings briefing.
- Duration: Fixed 30 calendar days from kickoff to final readout.
- Capacity Cap: Maximum 2 diagnostics per month.
- Execution: Shafiq Rahman conducts the work personally. No junior staff, no subcontractors.
- Exclusions: No retainer required. No hands-on software development or vendor implementation included.

## The Four Deliverables
1. AI Use Inventory & Risk Tiers — every AI tool/pilot found, tiered High / Medium / Low risk using NIST AI Risk Management Framework concepts, with owner, data used, and vendor named for each.
2. Kill / Scale / Fix List — a decision list for every pilot: stop it, scale it, or fix it first, with the reason in one sentence each.
3. 90-Day Governance Roadmap — who decides, what gets reviewed before purchase or go-live, and the 5 controls to put in place first.
4. Board One-Pager + 60-Minute Findings Briefing — a one-page summary for the board and a live briefing with the CEO/Board Chair.

## Engagement Timeline (Four Weeks)
- Week 1: Inventory — Shafiq interviews up to 5 people (CEO/COO, interim CIO/IT lead, CMIO or clinical lead, CISO/security lead, compliance/privacy lead), 45 minutes each, and reviews the AI tool list, vendor contracts, and existing policies the hospital provides.
- Week 2: Risk Tiering — Every item tiered; gaps in ownership, data use, and vendor terms flagged.
- Week 3: Draft Findings — Kill/Scale/Fix list and 90-day roadmap drafted; one 30-minute check-in with the sponsor.
- Week 4: Findings Briefing — 60-minute briefing + board one-pager delivered. Engagement ends.

## What the Hospital Must Provide
- List of AI tools in use, vendor contracts, current AI/data policies (if any), and access to the 5 interviewees. Total executive time asked: about 4 hours over 30 days.

## Leadership Biography
Shafiq Rahman, MS, MBA, MCS, PMP®, Former Maryland State CIO. State CIO / Chief Information & Digital Transformation Officer, Maryland Department of Transportation, October 2023–January 2026: led a $250M+ IT enterprise, ~1,500 staff across six agencies; co-authored Maryland's first statewide AI governance policy as a member of the Governor's AI Sub-cabinet; modernized mainframe systems to Microsoft Azure; rationalized ~850 applications to ~620, ~$6M in recurring annual savings. Director of Enterprise IT, University of Maryland School of Medicine, October 2014–October 2023: led the MEDITECH-to-Epic migration and clinical data interoperability across seven hospitals under HIPAA/HITECH. Founder & Principal, Nexis AI, March 2026–present. Author of "AI Governance: A Local Government Leader's Guide" (ICMA, March 2024).

## Higher Education & Academic Medical Center Advisory Practice
In addition to the hospital diagnostic, Nexis AI provides executive technology advisory for University Presidents, Provosts, Deans, and Interim CIOs:
- Institutional AI Governance & Academic Integrity Policies: Pragmatic policies balancing faculty research freedom, student learning integrity, and enterprise data privacy.
- Research Computing & High-Performance GPU Enclaves: Compliant Slurm clusters, biomedical computing enclaves, and sovereign grant infrastructure.
- Academic Health Science & Clinical Integration: Unifying network boundaries, IAM identity federation, and clinical EHR data flows (Epic/MEDITECH) between university campuses and teaching hospital networks.
- FERPA & Federal Research Compliance: Safeguarding student records under FERPA, clinical trials under HIPAA, and federal grants under NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC.
- Leadership Grounding: Shafiq Rahman served 9 years as Director of Enterprise IT at the University of Maryland School of Medicine, supporting ~3,000 faculty, ~3,000 staff, 1,300+ students, residents, and fellows across 25 academic departments.
